title: Actual grace: the good motions God stirs in us
source_text: XXVIII. Itaque ad gratiam actualem pertinent, ex doctorum Scholae Romanae sententia, omnes boni & salutares motus, quos in animis nostris Deus excitat. Qui motus & Dei sunt, quoniam ab eo procedunt: & nostri quoque, quoniam sunt actiones vitales, a facultatibus nostris, Deo speciali modo movente, elicitae.
pass_a_gloss: XXVIII. And so to actual grace pertain, from the opinion of the doctors of the Roman School, all the good and salutary motions, which God excites in our minds. Which motions are both God's, because they proceed from him: and ours also, because they are vital actions, elicited from our faculties, God moving in a special manner.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXVIII. In the view of the doctors of the Roman School, then, actual grace covers all the good and saving motions God stirs up in our souls.
These motions are God's, because they come from him. They are ours too, because they are vital acts drawn out of our own faculties as God moves them in a special way.

lemmas.gloss: all the good and salutary motions, which God excites in our minds
elicited, God moving in a special manner

choices.why: Acts that come from within a living agent's own powers; so the motions are truly ours even though God moves them.
